title: Bar and Bat Mitzvah Planning Kit
subtitle: A 12 to 18 month plan for the service, the party, and everything in between
intro: A bar or bat mitzvah is a meaningful milestone and a big gathering at the same time. This kit helps you balance the religious service with the celebration, keep kids and adults comfortable, and stay on budget. Always follow your synagogue, rabbi, and family customs where they differ from this general guide.

sections.heading: 12 to 18 Month Timeline
sections.note: Synagogue dates and popular party venues often book more than a year ahead.

tasks: Meet with your synagogue to confirm the service date, study schedule, and requirements.
Talk with your child about what they want for the service and the party.
Set a total budget and decide who is contributing.
Choose possible party dates and tour venues.
Ask about kosher requirements at the synagogue and venue.
Start a master guest list with family, friends, and classmates.
Book the party venue and review the contract.
Reserve the caterer, or confirm that the venue provides kosher or kosher-style options.
Hire a DJ, band, or MC who has experience with mitzvah parties.
Book the photographer and videographer.
Start gathering photos for a slideshow.
Create a shared folder for contracts and contacts.
Choose a theme, color palette, and overall style.
Book entertainment such as photo booth, game stations, or activities for kids.
Plan a candle lighting ceremony and who will be honored.
Choose invitation designs and order them.
Discuss honors for the service, such as aliyot, and who will be asked.
Plan a family tikkun olam or community service project if desired.
Order rentals: tables, chairs, linens, and lounge furniture.
Schedule outfit shopping for the child and family.
Plan transportation and lodging for out-of-town guests.
Order centerpieces and decorations.
Plan the cake or dessert display.
Book hair and makeup if desired.
Mail invitations with an RSVP date about 4 weeks before the event.
Confirm the full day schedule from service to party.
Choose music for the entrance, candle lighting, hora, and other highlights.
Create a do-not-play list for the DJ.
Plan kids' activities and the adult dining experience.
Order favors and giveaways.
Track RSVPs and call people who have not replied.
Create a seating chart draft with kids and adults sections.
Print programs for the service.
Confirm all vendors and share the schedule.
Rehearse at the synagogue with the rabbi or cantor.
Prepare a thank-you speech or family remarks.
Give the final headcount to the venue and caterer.
Print place cards and table numbers.
Confirm rental delivery and setup times.
Pack an emergency kit with safety pins, tissues, water, and snacks.
Check the Chicago forecast and plan for coats and parking.
Prepare envelopes for vendor tips and payments.
Send thank-you notes within a few weeks.
Return rentals and attire on time.
Order prints, albums, or the final video.
Make donations or complete any planned service project.

sections.heading: Service Planning Checklist
sections.note: Your synagogue will guide the order and requirements of the service.

groups.title: Before the service
items: Confirm tallit, kippot, and any required attire.
Share the schedule with family and honored guests.
Ask about seating for the family and where honorees will sit.
Order printed programs or explanatory booklets for guests who may be unfamiliar.
Plan arrival and parking for guests.
Ask about photography rules inside the sanctuary.
Pack a bag with tissues, water, and a spare outfit.

groups.title: Honors and participation
items: List family members and friends who will receive honors.
Share instructions and practice materials with those honorees.
Plan a short speech or d'var Torah with your child.
Decide on a gift or blessing for the child.
Arrange for candy throwing if allowed by your synagogue.

groups.title: After the service
items: Plan a kiddush or reception right after the service.
Provide a transition plan from synagogue to party venue.
Allow time for photos and changing outfits.
Plan a break so the family can rest between events.
Plan winter coat storage and parking if the service is in colder months.

groups.title: Venue and flow
items: Choose a floor plan with dining, dancing, and a kids' area.
Plan the grand entrance and introduction.
Reserve a dance floor sized for guests.
Plan the candle lighting, hora, and toasts.
Schedule the cake cutting and desserts.
Leave enough quiet space for older guests.
Plan where gifts and cards will be collected securely.

groups.title: Food and drink
items: Confirm kosher or kosher-style requirements.
Plan kid-friendly foods and a separate station if desired.
Include vegetarian and allergy-friendly options.
Provide nonalcoholic drinks and mocktails.
Plan late-night snacks for the dance floor.
Label foods clearly.

groups.title: Entertainment
items: Book an MC who can engage both kids and adults.
Plan dance contests and group activities.
Include a photo booth or game stations.
Prepare a slideshow or video.
Create a playlist with input from the guest of honor.

groups.title: Rentals and setup
items: Confirm table count and sizes for the guest count.
Choose linens and chair styles to match the theme.
Reserve a dance floor, staging, and lighting.
Plan lounge seating for teens and a quiet area for grandparents.
Order table numbers, centerpieces, and place card stands.
Confirm load-in times and who will receive deliveries.

sections.heading: Kids Zone and Adult Zone
sections.note: Giving each group their own space helps everyone enjoy the party.
rows: Round tables near the dance floor with friends
Tables farther from the speakers, with extra chairs for grandparents
Kid-friendly menu, finger foods, snack station
Plated or buffet meal with adult beverages
Games, photo booth, dance floor, DJ contests
Quiet lounge area, cocktail space, conversation corners
Higher energy near the dance floor
Lower volume in the lounge and dining areas
Clearly signed and close to the dance floor

sections.heading: Rentals Table
sections.note: Rough planning guidelines. Your venue, floor plan, and guest mix will change the numbers.

sections.heading: Budget Split
sections.note: A starting point for planning. Costs vary widely by venue, guest count, and style.

lines.tip: Ask about kosher options, per-person pricing, and service charges.
Confirm the number of hours and any extra costs for lighting or sound.
Ask what is included for the service and the party.
Chairs, linens, dance floor, and lounge pieces make a big impact.
Include outfits for both the service and the party.
Digital invitations can cut costs while still looking polished.
Ask about any donation guidelines and program printing.
Group shuttle options can ease parking in Chicago.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask Vendors
items: Do you have experience with mitzvah parties and the service-to-party transition?
What kosher or kosher-style options are available, and is there a supervision fee?
How many hours does the package include, and how much is overtime?
Can you provide a separate kids' menu and station?
What time can rentals be delivered, and when will they be picked up?
Is a dance floor included, or does it need to be rented separately?
What is the policy for outside desserts or specialty items?
What is your cancellation and rescheduling policy?
